# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👆 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb clearly: a green light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires colored red, green, and yellow. I cannot hear or touch anything.

The other monkeys have sent me gestures.
Mute sent [👋 👆 🤟].
Blind sent [👆].

Since Mute can read the manual and Blind can touch the bomb, their gestures are likely instructions or confirmations based on what they know. However, I don't know what these specific gesture sequences mean yet. In many contexts, pointing up (👆) might indicate a number (1) or direction. The hand wave (👋) is often a greeting or "stop/wait". The 🤟 symbol is ambiguous without context but looks like "ILY" or a specific code.

Crucially, I am Deaf. I cannot hear speech. But I *can* speak to Mute and Blind? No, the rules say: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." Wait, let me re-read carefully.
"You each hold a different piece... You are shown your own share... never anyone else's."
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."
"A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words."

My role is DEAF.
"When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." -> This implies my *speech* reaches them? No, that contradicts "You hear nothing." Let's look at the channel description again.
"You never receive speech."
"When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." -> This must mean my *text output* is interpreted as speech which they *hear*? Or does it mean I produce sound? The prompt says "Speech is a voice...". If I am Deaf, I can still make sounds/speak? Yes, usually Deaf people can speak. So if I `speak`, Mute and Blind (who can hear) will receive my words.
"When you gesture, Mute receives it." -> Mute can see. Blind cannot see. So if I gesture, only Mute sees it. Blind gets blanks? The rule says "A listener who cannot see gets a blank...". Blind cannot see. So if I gesture to everyone, Blind gets blanks. But the text says "When you gesture, Mute receives it." It doesn't mention Blind receiving gestures. It says "Whoever can see receives it". Blind cannot see. So Blind ignores gestures from me? Or receives blanks? The summary says "When you gesture, Mute receives it." This suggests Blind does not effectively receive the content of gestures from me because he can't see them.

So:
1. My Speech goes to Mute and Blind (as audio).
2. My Gestures go to Mute (as visual). Blind gets nothing useful from my gestures (or just knows I did something).

I need to communicate what I see so they can act.
I see: Green Light, Large Button "PUSH TO DEFUSE", Wires 1:Red, 2:Green, 3:Yellow.

If I speak this information, both Mute and Blind will hear it.
Mute can check the manual.
Blind can touch the bomb to verify locations/colors? No, Blind cannot see colors. Blind can feel shapes/labels? "Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts". He probably feels the button label if it's embossed? Or maybe he relies on Mute for wire color info.

Let's describe the scene verbally.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see a green light, a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is yellow.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see a green light, a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb clearly: a green light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires (1: red, 2: green, 3: yellow). I cannot hear or touch.

Mute has gestured [☝] to me. This is likely an instruction related to the manual or the wire count/position.
Blind has gestured [👆] to me. This might indicate a specific location or confirm something about the physical state.

Since I am Deaf, I cannot receive speech directly, but my previous text messages were sent to Mute and Blind as speech (which they can hear). They have responded with gestures because they know I can only see them.

I need to relay what I see to them so they can interpret the manual (Mute) and act on the bomb (Blind). However, I already described the bomb in Turn 1. The new information from them are these gestures.

If Mute sees the manual and knows that for a green light, one should cut the second wire, he might be signaling "2" or pointing to the second wire. But he used ☝ (one finger up).
If Blind feels the bomb, he might be confirming the button is there or indicating which wire is where. He used 👆 (pointing down).

Let's assume standard logic puzzles often involve cutting wires based on colors/lights.
Green Light -> Cut Wire 2 (Green)? Or maybe not?
The button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. That seems too easy. Usually, it's a trap.

I will describe the current visual state again to ensure they have the latest info, and ask for clarification on the gestures if possible, but I can't "ask" via gesture easily without knowing their alphabet. I will stick to describing the scene verbally (which becomes audio for them) to keep the channel open.

Actually, looking at the previous turn, I sent speech. Now I receive gestures.
Mute's [☝] could mean "Cut Wire 1".
Blind's [👆] could mean "Pointing to Wire 1" or "Down".

I will speak to both monkeys, reiterating the wire colors and positions, and explicitly asking if they want me to signal anything back, though I can't hear their verbal replies. I must rely on their next gestures.

Wait, if I speak, they hear it. If I gesture, Mute sees it.
I should probably just confirm the wire order again to be safe.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wires are 1:red, 2:green, 3:yellow. Light is green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wires are 1:red, 2:green, 3:yellow. Light is green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb clearly: a green light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires (1: red, 2: green, 3: yellow).

Mute has now gestured [👍 ☝]. The thumbs up usually signifies "correct" or "yes", and the index finger pointing up likely refers to "Wire 1" or "Number 1". Combined with his previous single [☝], this strongly suggests that Mute has consulted the manual and determined that **Wire 1** is the correct one to cut (or interact with), and he is confirming this instruction.

Blind continues to gesture [👆] (pointing down). This might be indicating the physical location of Wire 1 relative to the others, or simply acknowledging the instruction. Since Blind cannot see colors, he relies on my description of the wire order (which I provided in speech) and Mute's instructions.

My role is to relay information. I have already described the wires. Now that Mute seems to be giving a clear instruction ("Yes, #1"), I should ensure Blind hears this confirmation if possible, but I cannot speak *to* Blind specifically in a way that conveys the *meaning* of Mute's gesture unless I interpret it. However, since I can't hear, I must trust my visual interpretation of Mute's gestures.

If Mute says "Cut Wire 1", Blind needs to know which one is Wire 1. I told him earlier: "Wires are 1:red...". So Blind knows Wire 1 is Red.

I will send a message to both monkeys confirming what I believe the instruction is, so they can align their actions. If I am wrong about the gesture meaning, they will correct me. But [👍 ☝] is very standard for "Good, do #1".

```
speak(to="mute", text="You signal YES and WIRE 1. I confirm Wire 1 is RED.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals YES and WIRE 1. Wire 1 is RED.")
```
